statement: an UNREADABLE-yet-present op-log file (jsonl or .mzseg) THROWS OpLogStore.ReadError.unreadableFile naming the file (RULING-54, this branch) — it used to contribute zero ops with EMPTY diagnostics, so the document opened SHORTER with no quarantine record, the writer's next autosave truncated the .md to match, and the new sequence keyframe SUPERSEDED the file's paragraphs when it came back (text surviving in the log but never reappearing). Absent files still read as empty — the legitimate new-document state
reachability: LIVE — any permissions break, iCloud dataless stub, or squatting entry under .maugham/ops/

statement: a document whose op-log file set contains an unreadable file REFUSES to load, with the error naming the file and stating the words are intact inside it; the editor shows the refusal in the pane (EditorHost.loadError replaces the eternal 'Loading…' placeholder) and posts it as a project notice
reachability: LIVE — same failure shapes, at document open

statement: an ops directory that EXISTS but cannot be LISTED refuses the load (OpLogStore.verifyOpsDirectoryListable) — it used to read as 'no log yet' through the presence-only glob and send Bootstrap minting FRESH paragraph ids: a second, parallel history over the writer's intact one

the sync-merge read throws on an unreadable file too, so a CLOSED document — DerivedManuscript, and through it MCP read_document, search-adjacent readers and the compile pipeline — never silently derives a shorter manuscript; the compile path's Source protocol is throwing, so an unreadable file FAILS the compile through the DurableProgress catch instead of emitting a book missing chapters
reachability: LIVE — MCP reads of closed docs; every compile

scope: segment checksum vs unreadable — the two failure kinds
statement: a READABLE-but-corrupt segment (checksum/magic/decompress failure) still salvages decompressable lines and records a quarantine skip — partial truth, recorded — while an UNREADABLE segment throws: nothing can be known about it, so nothing can be honestly salvaged. Two different answers to two genuinely different questions

deliberately lenient after RULING-54, each with its reason in place: the app-fringe readers (search content, background word-count stats, closed-doc task derivation, the rename pre-check, the statement-preview classifier, the scenes sidebar, the project task log) read via try? and SKIP an unreadable doc — every one of them meets the loud refusal the moment the doc is opened, and none can mutate anything from the shortened view. Still queued: checkpoints (CheckpointStore.load — a device's checkpoints vanish silently), sealTailIfNeeded's silent skip, PendingBuffer's silent crash-recovery skip, and BackupSignature's dropped file
